claim: Gros & Devanbu's small white-box probes trained on generator-model internal activations achieve low calibration error and a Brier Skill Score of approximately 0.2 for predicting which code lines/spans will be edited in a minimal correctness-repairing patch, even when the probe is far smaller than the generator model it probes.
stance_target: feasibility and effectiveness of external probing for localized code-correctness confidence
scope_conditions: generated code from multiple generator model sizes, 'Minimal Intent Aligning Patches' dataset built via curated patch construction
quoted_support: Small probes achieve low calibration error and Brier Skill Score ~0.2 for predicting edited lines, even on code from generator models many orders of magnitude larger than the probe.

claim: Gros & Devanbu's 'localized' confidence is spatial/textual (per code line or span, indicating odds it will be edited in a minimal patch), fundamentally different from DPRC's per-test-case/per-requirement structuring; ground-truth comes from a curated repaired-patch dataset rather than reused execution outcomes, and the confidence estimator is an external white-box probe on model internals rather than the code LLM natively self-expressing its own confidence.
stance_target: DPRC's differentiation from the highest title-collision prior work
scope_conditions: comparison of localization axis, label source, and confidence-production mechanism
quoted_support: the localization axis is SPATIAL/TEXTUAL (which code lines/spans will be edited), not PER-TEST-CASE (which individual hidden test will pass) -- a fundamentally different structuring of 'localized confidence'

claim: A probe trained only on code shows some generalization to natural-language error localization, and white-box probing beats black-box reflective and self-consistency baselines for this localization task.
stance_target: cross-domain transfer potential of localized code-confidence signals
scope_conditions: code-trained probe evaluated on NL error localization transfer task
quoted_support: a probe trained only on code shows some generalization to natural-language error localization

claim: This paper represents the highest title-level scoop risk identified for DPRC and must be explicitly differentiated in related work: 'localized' confidence must be framed as per-test-case/per-requirement, not per-line/span, to avoid conflation.
quoted_support: This paper represents the highest title-level scoop risk found in this search and should be explicitly differentiated in the related-work section
